key_insight: OpenVLThinkerV2 adapts group-relative policy optimization to multimodal generalist models by explicitly addressing reward-topology variance and separating fine-grained perception from multi-step reasoning, enabling robust multi-domain visual task performance.
problem_solved: Extends GRPO-driven RL training to open-source multimodal generalist models by overcoming (1) extreme variance in reward landscapes across diverse visual tasks and (2) the trade-off between detailed visual perception and long-horizon multimodal reasoning.
method: Task-aware GRPO extensions: normalize and group rewards across task families to stabilize policy updates under heterogeneous reward topologies.

Modular perception–reasoning architecture: specialized visual encoder + task-conditioned reasoning module with cross-modal attention to retain fine-grained perception while supporting multi-step inference.
Multi-domain training strategy: curriculum and grouped optimization across visual tasks to improve generalization and reduce catastrophic interference.
impact: Provides a practical, reproducible approach for fine-tuning open-source multimodal models with RL that balances perception and reasoning, making it easier for practitioners to build generalist visual agents across many tasks without bespoke tuning for each task.

paper_title: OpenVLThinkerV2: A Generalist Multimodal Reasoning Model for Multi-domain Visual Tasks
paper_authors: Wenbo Hu, Xin Chen, Yan Gao-Tian, Yihe Deng, Nanyun Peng
